about: What Hiveku's social_post_strategy_check route answers for this dataset, recorded 2026-11-15 by running the route's own check on each body below with this dataset as the account (the ICP, the journey and its linked ICP, the grid and its ICP, the pillar, the brand guide's phrases to avoid, the public testimonials, and each network's last 20 posts that went out or will).
Each item is 'id[:platform] | status | reason'; a stage's job is jobs[stage.awareness]; platforms are the networks of target_platforms and target_accounts.
tools.mjs answers the same (the self-test holds it to this file). Record it again when the route changes.

body.content: Myth: the lacquer failed. Truth: the coat under it was never sanded. Of 312 doors through our finish room in July, the 4 that came back had skipped the 320 pass between coats on one rush order. The 41 Harlow Street doors got the pass and are 18 months in with zero call-backs. Ask your shop what happens between coats, then save this for the next finish schedule you sign.

body.content: We used to skip the sand between coats on rush jobs. Then 4 doors from one July kitchen came back with the top coat lifting at the seams, and the fix cost more than the day we saved. Every coat gets the 320 pass now, rush or not, and the 41 Harlow Street doors are 18 months in with zero call-backs. Comment with the finish failure you see most and we will answer it in the next post.
